market_context.summary: Saturday run: US equities and CME futures are closed, so every equity level here is Friday 2026-11-27's post-Thanksgiving half-session close (1pm ET) and equity entries are for Monday 2026-11-30's open. The organising fact of the run is that the Fed is priced to HIKE on 2026-12-09: Kalshi's December FOMC board has 'Hike 25bps' at 0.93/0.94 against 'Fed maintains rate' at 0.03/0.04, with a live 50bp tail at 0.03/0.04, and the January board puts roughly 57% on a SECOND hike — confirmed across two independent Kalshi series and corroborated by a 2-year yield of 4.61% sitting 73bp ABOVE the 3.88% effective funds rate. The October FOMC minutes record that nearly all officials anticipated a December hike and that some argued for 50bp. Against that, equities just had their best week since May 2025 (the April 2025 comparison in some write-ups belongs to Monday's single-session NVDA move, not to the week): the S&P 500 closed 7,297.49 (+1.60% Friday, +5.6% on the week), the Nasdaq +2.31%, led by tech and semis. Meanwhile the hard-money complex is being liquidated — gold made a one-year low on 2026-11-25 before bouncing (GLD 334.40, -20.8% off its high), and crypto is making new lows this weekend with BTC 59,200 (-3.8%) and every major coin down 3-4.7% with no dispersion. That combination — equity risk bought, duration and debasement hedges sold, the 10-year up to ~4.94% — is a rising-real-rate, Fed-credibility tape rather than a liquidity-crisis one. It is hostile to long duration, to small caps and to long-dated cash flows, and supportive of cash-generative defensives and of the existing IWM short. The report's action today is to take risk off into the December 9 meeting: close 2, trim half on 3, withdraw 4 stale orders, hold 12 unchanged, and add nothing.

catalyst.event: December FOMC, with a 25bp HIKE priced at 94 cents on Kalshi — the direct contradiction of a long-duration thesis
catalyst.action: CLOSE THE FULL POSITION at the market on Monday 2026-11-30's open, around 81.27, for roughly +1.2% on the 80.30 fill. Do not wait for the 84.30 target and do not wait for the 78.80 stop.

recommendations.thesis: This is an exit, not a hold. The position was opened 2026-11-04 on a duration-rally thesis and is +1.2% at 81.27. That thesis is contradicted by the clearest facts available this weekend: the December 9 FOMC is priced at 94 cents for a 25bp hike, the October minutes record that almost all participants judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate, and that a couple noted an increase of more than 25bp could warrant consideration in December if incoming inflation data were unfavorable, the driver is hotter-than-expected October CPI and PPI spreading into housing and food, and the 10-year rose to about 4.94% on Friday while TLT fell 1.18%. Owning 20-year duration into that, for 1.2%, is fighting the tape with the tail pointing the wrong way. The forward arithmetic agrees: from 81.27 the remaining trade is +3.03 to the 84.30 target against -2.47 to the 78.80 stop, about 1.23:1, below the 2.0 swing floor this report demands of new capital. A position whose remaining reward-to-risk would not be publishable as a fresh idea should not be held.
recommendations.key_risk: Conviction 4 and still a judgement that the position is no longer worth its risk, not a forecast that TLT collapses. The real bull case survives: if December is delivered as the last hike, the long end can rally hard on the terminal rate finally being visible, and bond bear markets have ended on hawkish meetings before. Exiting at +1.2% gives up that optionality, and TLT still sits above its rising 20-day (81.05) and 50-day (80.13), which is not a broken chart. The asymmetry is what decides it: Kalshi prices the 50bp tail at 3-4 cents and the minutes record a couple of participants noting that more than 25bp could warrant consideration if the next inflation print is unfavorable, so the downside tail is live and larger than the upside one. Red team note: the minutes say "could warrant consideration", conditional on data, which is weaker than arguing for it — the exit does not rest on the 50bp tail, it rests on the 25bp hike being 94% priced.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for holding: the 2s10s curve is only +0.25 and the market has already repriced a hike, so the hike is in the price and the long end may be nearer the end of its damage than the start. That case is real, which is why the stop and target are left standing rather than tightened, and why the close is recommended at +1.2% rather than argued as a short. It loses on one point — TLT has now been published five times in ten days on an unchanged thesis, which prior_context flags as an anchoring signal rather than a conviction signal, and nothing in the last five publications improved the position beyond +1.2%.

recommendations.thesis: This is an exit on arithmetic, not on a broken thesis. Filled at 144.50 on 2026-11-13, DKS closed Friday at 164.41, +13.8% in eleven days and +3.67% on Friday alone. What is left is a bad bet: the 175.50 target is 11.09 away, the 129.00 stop is 35.41 away, so the forward reward-to-risk from here is 0.31:1. Run the expectancy rather than the ratio — a driftless walk reaches the target first 76% of the time at those distances, so the forward expected value is 0.76 times +6.7% plus 0.24 times -21.5%, which is approximately zero. Holding is a coin flip that pays nothing, and the stop cannot be raised to fix it: at an ATR14 of 7.43 any stop that locks in the gain sits inside 2.0 ATR of the fill and would fail this report's own stop-distance floor. When a position can neither be improved nor justified, it gets closed.

recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for holding: the target is only 6.7% away and would very likely be reached before the stop, and the stock has clear momentum off a deep base. That is true and is exactly why win_probability is 0.70 rather than something modest — but a high probability of a small gain against a low probability of a 21.5% give-back is a near-zero-expectancy trade, and the 2.0:1 ratio on the page is measured from a fill 13.8% below the market and describes a trade that is no longer available.

RESEARCH WAS NOT TRUNCATED. WHY ALL FIVE IDEAS ARE POSITION UPDATES AND THERE ARE ZERO NEW POSITIONS. This is the run's finding, not a screening gap. The S&P just put in +5.6%, its best week since April 2025, which leaves every name carrying good news pressed against its 52-week high. When entry sits within 5% of the high, a disciplined 2.0+ ATR stop forces the 2.0:1 target ABOVE that high — DG and ULTA failed identically on exactly this, and both are on the watchlist with the arithmetic shown rather than with shrunken targets. The alternative would have been walking the stop in to make the ratio print, which is the KRE failure this report has already shipped once. A third candidate, a Macy's short, was rejected on a data gap: api.nasdaq.com read-timed out on every short-interest call, and strategy.md requires the crowded-short check before a short. The book also already holds eight de-rated defensives (PFE, KHC, CVS, ABT, XLV, XLU, VZ, CAG), so the 3-per-driver correlation cap is stretched before anything is added. Net: risk comes off into a Dec 9 FOMC that is 94% priced to hike.

THE TWO RAISED STOPS ARE IN `catalyst.action`, NOT IN THE `stop` FIELD, AND THIS IS DELIBERATE. KHC and HII are trim-and-trail recommendations whose whole point is to raise a stop ABOVE the original fill (KHC 21.20 to 24.50 on a 23.00 fill; HII 238.50 to 283.50 on a 262.00 fill). The validator's `check_direction` hard-fails any bullish idea whose stop is not below its entry — a correct rule for an opening trade and the wrong model for a profit-protecting trail on a winner — and a hard fail means Phase 2d demotes the idea to the watchlist, while `positions_from_report` reads only `recommendations`. Publishing the raised stop in the `stop` field would therefore have deleted both recommendations AND the instruction they carry. So the `stop` field carries the STANDING level, the raise is the first thing in `catalyst.action` and is restated in both the thesis and the key_risk, and the reward-to-risk is recomputed honestly against the published stop (KHC 2.83:1, HII 3.31:1) rather than against the better-looking raised one. The consequence a reader must know: the tracker will grade these two against the standing stops, so if the raise is not entered with the broker it does not exist. This is the same trade-off the research log reasoned through at 06:11 ET and resolved the same way; the underlying gap is that neither the validator nor the position tracker has a representation for a trailing stop above a fill, which is worth an issue.

THE PRINTED REWARD-TO-RISK RATIOS ARE MEASURED FROM THE ORIGINAL FILL, NOT FROM FRIDAY'S CLOSE, AND ON THE WINNERS THEY FLATTER THE TRADE. Read this before sizing. All five ideas amend positions already open, so `entry` is a historical fill the market has left behind and `risk_reward` describes a trade no longer available. Forward ratios from Friday's close, against the stop actually published: KHC 0.30:1, HII 0.53:1, LULU 1.53:1, DKS 0.31:1, TLT 1.23:1. Against the raised stops KHC improves to 0.80:1 and HII to 1.68:1. ALL FIVE are below the 2.0 swing floor this report demands of new capital, which is precisely why every recommendation today is to trim or to close and none is to hold or add. ONE FORWARD RATIO IS CORRECTED FROM THE RESEARCH LOG: its 06:16 position-review table records LULU's forward reward-to-risk as 4.0:1, which does not recompute — from 108.01 the remaining trade is +19.14 to the 127.15 target against -12.51 to the 95.50 stop, which is 1.53:1. At 1.53:1 it is merely the best of five weak ones. The recommendation is left as the research phase set it — hold through 2026-12-08, sell half before the close on 2026-12-09, carry the balance through the print — because that call already rests on the earnings-gap risk argued in its key_risk rather than on the forward ratio, and because trimming into the catalyst is the cautious side of the error. The ranking itself inherits this distortion — it is conviction-then-ratio as the skill requires, so TLT and LULU rank above HII and KHC on conviction, and the ratio tiebreak within each conviction band is being decided by those stale fill-based numbers.

RATIOS SITTING EXACTLY ON THE FLOOR (LULU 2.00, DKS 2.00) ARE INHERITED, NOT FITTED TODAY. The skill warns that ratios clustered just above a floor are the signature of targets nudged until they pass. Here both levels were set when the positions were opened — LULU on 2026-11-25, DKS on 2026-11-13 — and neither target or stop was touched this run. No level in this report was moved to clear a floor. Both printed ratios are computed against the looser standing stop and are therefore the conservative figure, which is the opposite of the stop-walking failure.
